intro: The Litter-Robot 4 signals almost every fault through the status light, so start there. Blue is a pause, yellow is the drawer, red is a stop. Nearly every red-light call we can find in owner reports comes down to overfilled litter or a drawer that is not fully seated.

symptoms.title: Flashing blue light
symptoms.summary: The status light pulses blue rather than sitting solid.
causes: A cycle is paused because the cat sensor is still triggered.
The unit is in the middle of its post-visit countdown.
Something is resting on the globe and holding the weight sensor active.

fixes.detail: A pulsing blue light during the delay period is normal behaviour, not a fault.

fixes.step: Clear the top of the unit
fixes.detail: A towel, a cat bed or a second cat sitting on the bonnet will hold the sensor triggered indefinitely.
If blue persists with nothing on the unit, unplug for 30 seconds.

symptoms.escalate: Continuous pulsing blue with an empty, level unit points to a weight sensor fault — a warranty item.

symptoms.title: Flashing red light
symptoms.summary: Red is the fault code. The unit has stopped and will not resume on its own.
causes: The globe is obstructed or has not returned to its home position.
The drawer is out or not fully seated.
Over-torque protection has tripped, usually from packed or overfilled litter.

fixes.detail: Unplug, remove the globe, and look for a jam at the sifting screen or the drop zone.
Remove litter down to the fill line before restarting. Over-filling is the usual cause of an over-torque trip.
Refit the globe, seat the drawer until it clicks, then plug in and let it home itself.

symptoms.escalate: Red that returns immediately after a clean restart is a motor or control-board fault. Do not keep resetting it — open a warranty case.

symptoms.title: Flashing yellow light
symptoms.summary: Yellow indicates the drawer needs attention.
causes: The waste drawer is full.
The drawer is not seated.
The drawer sensor is dusty and reading full.

fixes.detail: Empty the drawer, wipe the sensor window, and push the drawer home until it clicks.
Press and hold the reset so the fill count clears.

symptoms.escalate: Yellow with an empty, clean, correctly seated drawer is a sensor fault.

symptoms.title: Cycle interrupted
symptoms.summary: The cycle starts and then reverses or aborts partway.
causes: The cat re-entered mid-cycle. This is the safety system doing its job.
A clump has jammed against the sifting screen.
The unit is on an unstable surface and the weight reading fluctuates during rotation.

fixes.step: Confirm it is not the cat
fixes.detail: Check the app cycle log. An interruption immediately followed by a visit entry is normal safety behaviour.
Power off and scrape any welded clump from the screen and drop zone.
Move the unit off carpet or a flexing floorboard onto a solid, level surface.

symptoms.escalate: Repeated interruptions with no cat present and a clean screen indicate a sensor fault.

symptoms.title: Will not cycle
symptoms.summary: The unit sits idle after a visit, or starts and immediately stops without completing a cycle.
causes: Too much litter. Overfilling past the fill line is the single most common cause of a failed cycle.
A clump has welded to the sifting screen or the drum wall and is jamming rotation.
The waste drawer is not seated fully, so the safety interlock keeps the motor disabled.

fixes.detail: Litter should sit at or just below the marked fill line. If in doubt, remove a cup and try again.
Pull the waste drawer fully out and push it back until it clicks. A drawer that is 5 mm proud will stop the cycle.
Power off, remove the globe or drum, and scrape any welded clumps off the sifting screen with a plastic scraper.
With the litter removed, run one cycle. If it completes empty and fails when loaded, the problem is litter or weight, not the motor.

symptoms.escalate: A unit that fails an empty test cycle has a motor, gear or control-board fault and needs warranty service. Stop using it.

symptoms.title: Cat weight readings are wrong
symptoms.summary: The app reports a weight that is clearly wrong, jumps between visits, or attributes visits to the wrong cat.
causes: The unit is not on a level floor. Weight sensing assumes level.
Litter has been added or removed without re-taring, so the baseline is stale.
Something is resting against the unit — a wall, a mat edge, a cable — and taking part of the load.

fixes.detail: Use a phone level on the base. Even a small tilt on an uneven floor throws readings off by a pound or more.
Run the calibration or re-zero routine in the app whenever you add or fully change litter.
Leave two inches around the unit and keep it off thick rugs, which flex under load.
Weight-based identification cannot reliably separate two cats within about a pound of each other. Tag visits by hand if that is your situation.

symptoms.escalate: If readings are still erratic on a level floor after re-taring, the load cell is likely faulty and is a warranty item.

symptoms.title: Drawer shows full when it is not
symptoms.summary: The app or the indicator light insists the waste drawer is full immediately after you emptied it.
causes: Waste is packed against the sensor window rather than spread across the drawer.
The sensor window is dusty. Litter dust builds a film that reads as full.
The liner is bunched up over the sensor.

fixes.detail: Find the small clear window inside the drawer bay and wipe it with a dry microfibre cloth. Do this monthly.
Use the reset in the app or the physical drawer button so the counter clears after emptying.
Tuck the bag so it lies against the drawer walls rather than ballooning across the sensor line.

symptoms.escalate: A sensor that reads full with the drawer removed entirely is faulty and is a warranty item.

symptoms.title: Shows offline in the app
symptoms.summary: The unit works but the Whisker app shows it as offline, or commands from the app do nothing.
causes: The box is on a 5 GHz network segment. Almost every litter box on the market is 2.4 GHz only.
The router moved the unit to a different band after a firmware update or a mesh node reshuffle.
The box sits behind an appliance or in a metal-lined cabinet that kills the signal.

fixes.detail: Confirm your phone is on the 2.4 GHz network when you pair. On a combined-band router, temporarily split the bands or use the guest 2.4 GHz network.
Unplug the box for 30 seconds, then reboot the router, then plug the box back in. Order matters — the box looks for the network on boot.
Signal strength at floor level behind a washing machine is far worse than it looks. Try the unit in the open before concluding the radio is faulty.
Remove the device from the app entirely, then run setup again rather than retrying the existing entry.

symptoms.escalate: If it pairs and drops within minutes repeatedly, that is a hardware or firmware fault — contact Whisker rather than continuing to re-pair.

symptoms.title: Wi-Fi setup fails during pairing
symptoms.summary: Setup runs to the last step and then reports a failure, or the app never finds the unit.
causes: Phone is on 5 GHz while the box needs 2.4 GHz.
The Wi-Fi password contains characters the unit rejects, or the network name is hidden.
Location or local-network permission is denied to the Whisker app, so it cannot see the device.

fixes.detail: Both Location and Local Network permissions must be allowed for pairing to work on iOS. Android needs Location.
Broadcast a plain, visible 2.4 GHz network with an alphanumeric password for setup. You can move it afterwards.

fixes.step: Stay within six feet during pairing
fixes.detail: Pairing uses a short-range handshake before the box joins the network.

symptoms.escalate: If pairing fails on a known-good 2.4 GHz network from two different phones, the radio module is faulty.

symptoms.title: It still smells
symptoms.summary: The box cycles normally but the room smells worse than expected — often starting a few weeks in.
causes: The carbon filter is past its life. Filters degrade quietly; there is no warning.
The drawer gasket has litter dust on the seal face, so the drawer no longer closes airtight.
Litter depth is too shallow, so urine reaches the drum wall instead of clumping.
The unit needs a full wash. Waste film builds on the drum wall and no amount of cycling removes it.

fixes.detail: Set a recurring reminder rather than waiting to notice. Whisker filters are a running cost, not an optional accessory.
Wipe the drawer seal and the mating face with a damp cloth, then dry. A gritty seal leaks.
Run to the fill line, not below it. Shallow litter is the most common cause of odor in an otherwise healthy unit.
Strip the unit, wash the drum and drawer with unscented soap and warm water, dry completely before reassembly.

symptoms.escalate: Persistent ammonia smell despite all of the above can indicate a cat health issue. It is worth a vet conversation, not just a cleaning routine.
